blocks.v: 2 V to 6 V · Wide operating range
±4 mA at 5V · Can drive up to 10 LSTTL loads
SH/LD · Shift/Load (Active LOW). Loads parallel data when LOW; shifts when HIGH.
CLK · Clock Input. Shifts data on LOW-to-HIGH transition.
CLK INH · Clock Inhibit. When HIGH, clock is disabled.

blocks.text: Loading Data: Pull SH/LD (Pin 1) LOW to load the 8 parallel inputs (A–H) into the register. Data is loaded asynchronously (independent of the clock) .
Shifting Data: Pull SH/LD HIGH and CLK INH LOW, then pulse the CLK pin. Data shifts toward the serial output (QH) on each rising edge .
Cascading: Connect the QH output of one chip to the SER input of the next chip to chain multiple registers for 16, 24, or more inputs .
Unused Inputs: All unused inputs must be tied to VCC or GND to prevent floating CMOS inputs and erratic behavior .

uge-164790.summary: PCB For DIY Line Tracking Car

blocks.text: PCB For DIY Line Tracking Car
a DIY simple line-Tracking and obstacle-avoiding car, requiring the use of digital circuits to implement the tracking function and analog circuits to implement the obstacle avoidance function.

According to the design requirements, a 74HC00N NAND gate is used in conjunction with an infrared emitting tube. By judging whether infrared light is detected, the receiving tube is turned on or not, and the signal is input into the NAND gate to realize digital circuit tracking.

Using the LM393 comparator with the infrared emitting tube, it is also to determine whether the infrared light is detected in front and whether the receiving tube is turned on. The two sets of signals are input into the comparator for comparison to realize the obstacle avoidance function of the analog circuit.

The device is powered by two AA batteries, each with a voltage of 1.5V. Connecting two batteries in series provides a voltage of 3V, meeting the chip’s minimum power requirements. A three-position slide switch allows for switching between tracking and obstacle avoidance functions. Capacitors C1 and C3 are filter capacitors for energy storage. When the motor starts operating, transient currents are high, and the 100uF capacitor helps discharge the batteries.

The positive pole of the battery is connected to the positive pole of the motor, and the negative pole is controlled and turned on through a transistor. When a digital tracking or analog obstacle avoidance signal is generated, the base of the transistor is controlled to control the operation of the left and right tires, thereby realizing the tracking and obstacle avoidance functions.
U2 and U3 are infrared emitting tubes, and LED3 and LED4 are corresponding infrared receiving tubes, which are installed on both sides of the front wheels. The principle analysis is as follows:

When the car starts to move and hits the white paper, the infrared light is reflected and received by the receiving tube, which turns on. When it hits the black line, the infrared light is absorbed and the receiving tube turns off.
74HC00N is a NAND gate. When it touches the black line, the receiving tube is cut off, CNT1 outputs a high level, corresponding to OUT1 outputs a low level, and OUT3 outputs a high level;
At this time, the high level output by OUT3 will flow through the motor transistor, controlling the three-stage conduction and the motor rotation;
The vehicle continuously encounters black and white lines on the map route, thereby continuously turning on and off the transistor, realizing the line patrol function around the black line track.

IR1 and IR2 are infrared transmitting tubes, and CGQ1 and CGQ2 are corresponding infrared receiving tubes, which are installed on both sides of the front of the vehicle. The schematic diagram is analyzed as follows:

When the vehicle is running, there is no obstacle in front, the infrared transmission signal will not be received, the receiving tube is cut off, the 393 comparator’s non-inverting input terminal is the battery voltage, and the voltage is greater than the inverting input terminal. At this time, the 393 comparator outputs a high level to control the vehicle to move forward.

When there is an obstacle in front of the car, the infrared emission signal is received by the receiving tube, the receiving tube is turned on, 393 is relatively strong, the same-direction input end is low level, and the voltage is less than the inverting input end. At this time, 393 comparator outputs a low level, the corresponding wheel stops running, thereby achieving steering.

blocks.text: Alpha Plus board Arduino Uno Compatible for Robotics Development and DIY Projects

The UGE Alpha PLUS is an enhanced, Arduino UNO-compatible development board designed for DIY robotics and other creative projects. Built around the ATMega328P microcontroller with an UNO bootloader, it integrates various peripherals to save time and maximize productivity. The onboard CH340C USB-to-UART chip facilitates seamless code uploading and serial communication.
USB Interface: CH340C for easy code uploads and communication.
Power Options: USB, 7-12V DC Terminal Connector, or DC Jack.
Motor Control: Built-in L293DD dual motor driver for two motors plus an auxiliary motor.
Connectivity: Bluetooth, NRF24L01, I2C/OLED headers, and dedicated sensor headers (ultrasonic, IR, flame, servo).
IR Receiver: 38KHz with jumper for connection control.
Pin Headers: Rich analog and digital headers with power pins.
Power Options: Equipped with DC jack and terminal block for flexible power input, with reverse polarity protection via a diode. A 78M05 regulator supplies stable current.
USB to UART: Built-in CH340C USB-to-UART converter with TX/RX indicator LEDs for programming ease.
Arduino UNO Compatibility: Same form factor and female headers as the Arduino UNO, ensuring shield compatibility while managing shared pins for onboard peripherals.
Easy Sensor Connections: All ATmega328 GPIO pins are routed to color-coded male headers with Signal, VCC, and GND, allowing easy sensor connections without expansion shields.
Configurable Buzzer: Buzzer connected to D2 with a jumper, allowing enable/disable functionality.
Infrared (IR) Receiver: 38kHz IR receiver on A2 with a jumper for connection control.
OLED Display Header: 4-pin header for OLED display on A4 (SDA) and A5 (SCL) for I2C.
Bluetooth Module Header: 4-pin header for HC-05 Bluetooth module on D0 (RX) and D1 (TX). Remove during programming to avoid UART conflict.
Dual DC Motor Driver: L293DD motor driver for two DC motors.
Motor Speed Control: EN1 (D3) for Motor1 and EN2 (D5) for Motor2 using PWM with analogWrite().
Motor Direction Control: Motor1 direction via D6 and Motor2 direction via D7, with NOT gate logic to save pins.

Auxiliary Motor Driver Output: A medium-power NPN transistor is connected to D2 (shared with the buzzer) for driving auxiliary DC loads (motors, pumps, solenoids, lamps). A dedicated 2-pin jumper enables/disables the output.
NRF24L01 Wireless Header: Header for NRF24L01 wireless transceiver module, enabling wireless communication with other boards or RC remotes that use the NRF24 module.

UGE Alpha PLUS is perfect for makers, hobbyists, and students working on robotics, automation, and IoT projects. The board’s extensive peripheral support allows for quick prototyping and flexible integration of various modules and sensors. Whether controlling motors, reading sensor data, or adding wireless connectivity, UGE UNO PLUS offers a versatile platform for a wide range of creative applications.
UGE UNO PLUS Getting Started Guide
Download and install the latest version of the Arduino IDE from the official website.
Ensure that the CH340C driver is installed to allow communication between your UGE UNO PLUS and your computer. The driver can be found here for different operating systems.
Use a USB cable to connect your UGE Alpha PLUS to your computer.
The board can also be powered via the DC Jack (7-12V) or the Terminal Connector if needed.
Go to Tools > Board and select “Arduino Uno.”
Go to Tools > Port and choose the appropriate COM port for your board.
In the Arduino IDE, go to File > Examples > Basics > Blink.
Click the “Upload” button to upload the sketch to your board.
The onboard LED (usually connected to pin 13) should start blinking.
Motor Control: Connect motors to the L293DD motor driver terminals, and use the relevant Arduino pins (as per the onboard labeling) to control motor speed and direction.
Bluetooth: Attach a Bluetooth module to the dedicated 4-pin header. Use the UART pins for communication (TX/RX).
IR Remote: The IR receiver is connected to a specific digital pin. Include the IRremote library in your sketch to use this feature.
Sensors: Connect sensors to the dedicated 3-pin headers (GND-VCC-SIG) and use corresponding analog/digital pins in your sketches.
Connect an OLED display or any I2C device to the 4-pin I2C header.
Use the Wire library for I2C communication.
Plug the NRF24L01 module into the dedicated header.
Use the RF24 library to communicate with other NRF24L01 devices.
Write your own Arduino code or modify existing examples to suit your project.
Test the code by uploading and monitoring the serial output using the Arduino IDE’s Serial Monitor.
The board includes an onboard AMS1117 LDO regulator providing 3.3V. Ensure your peripherals do not exceed the 800mA limit.
Experiment with controlling the onboard buzzer and IR receiver via their respective jumpers.
Use the available pin headers for quick prototyping and sensor integration.

The STM32G431x6/x8/xB devices are based on the high-performance Arm® Cortex®-M4 32-bit RISC core. They operate at a frequency of up to 170 MHz.

The Cortex-M4 core features a single-precision floating-point unit (FPU), which supports all the Arm single-precision data-processing instructions and all the data types. It also implements a full set of DSP (digital signal processing) instructions and a memory protection unit (MPU) which enhances the application’s security.

These devices embed high-speed memories (up to 128 Kbytes of Flash memory, and 32 Kbytes of SRAM), an extensive range of enhanced I/Os and peripherals connected to two APB buses, two AHB buses and a 32-bit multi-AHB bus matrix.
The devices also embed several protection mechanisms for embedded Flash memory and SRAM: readout protection, write protection, securable memory area and proprietary code readout protection.
The devices embed peripherals allowing mathematical/arithmetic function acceleration (CORDIC for trigonometric functions and FMAC unit for filter functions).

They offer two fast 12-bit ADCs (4 Msps), four comparators, three operational amplifiers, four DAC channels (2 external and 2 internal), an internal voltage reference buffer, a low-power RTC, one general-purpose 32-bit timers, two 16-bit PWM timers dedicated to motor control, seven general-purpose 16-bit timers, and one 16-bit low-power timer.
They also feature standard and advanced communication interfaces such as:
– Three SPIs multiplexed with two half duplex I2Ss
– Three USARTs, one UART and one low-power UART.

The devices operate in the -40 to +85 °C (+105 °C junction) and -40 to +125 °C (+130 °C junction) temperature ranges from a 1.71 to 3.6 V power supply. A comprehensive set of power-saving modes allows the design of low-power applications.

blocks.text: NE556 General Purpose Dual Timer 5V 6mA IC DIP-14

The NE556 is a highly versatile dual timer integrated circuit that combines two independent 555 timer circuits within a single 14-pin package. It is designed for generating accurate timing intervals, pulse-width modulation signals, oscillations, and waveform generation in a wide variety of electronic systems. The device can operate in both monostable (one-shot) and a stable (oscillator) modes, making it suitable for timing and control applications ranging from microseconds to several hours.

With its ability to source or sink substantial output current and operate over a wide supply voltage range, the NE556 is widely used in industrial controls, alarm systems, LED flashers, tone generators, PWM motor control circuits, and electronic instrumentation. Integrating two timers into a single package reduces component count, saves PCB space, and simplifies circuit design while maintaining the reliability and flexibility that made the 555 timer family one of the most popular timing solutions in electronics.

These devices are precision timing circuits capable of producing accurate time delays or oscillation. In the time-delay or mono-stable mode of operation, the timed interval is controlled by a single external resistor and capacitor network. In the a-stable mode of operation, the frequency and duty cycle can be controlled independently with two external resistors and a single external capacitor. The threshold and trigger levels normally are two-thirds and one-third, respectively, of VCC. These levels can be altered by use of the control voltage terminal. When the trigger input falls below the trigger level, the flip-flop is set, and the output goes high. If the trigger input is above the trigger level and the threshold input is above the threshold level, the flip flop is reset and the output is low. The reset (RESET) input can override all other inputs and can be used to initiate a new timing cycle. When RESET goes low, the flip-flop is reset, and the output goes low. When the output is low, a low-impedance path is provided between discharge (DISCH) and ground. The output circuit is capable of sinking or sourcing current up to 200 mA. Operation is specified for supplies of 5 V to 15 V. With a 5-V supply, output levels are compatible with TTL inputs.

The ULN2003 is a monolithic IC consists of seven NPN darlington transistor pairs with high voltage and current capability. It is commonly used for applications such as relay drivers, motor, display drivers, led lamp drivers, logic buffers, line drivers, hammer drivers and other high voltage current applications. It consists of common cathode clamp diodes for each NPN darlington pair which makes this driver IC useful for switching inductive loads.
Schematic Diagram of each Darlington Pair – ULN2003

The output of the driver is open collector and the collector current rating of each darlington pair is 500mA. Darlington pairs may be paralleled if higher current is required. The driver IC also consists of a 2.7KΩ base resistor for each darlington pair. Thus each darlington pair can be operated directly with TTL or 5V CMOS devices. This driver IC can be used for high voltage applications up to 50V.

Note that the driver provides open collector output, so it can only sink current, cannot source. Thus when a 5V is given to 1B terminal, 1C terminal will be connected to ground via darlington pair and the maximum current that it can handle is 500A. From the above logic diagram we can see that cathode of protection diodes are shorted to 9th pin called COM. So for driving inductive loads, it must connected to the supply voltage. Datasheet

Note: Complete Technical Details can be found at the BD136 transistor datasheet given at the end of this page.

BD136 is a PNP transistor hence the collector and emitter will be closed (Forward biased) when the base pin is held at ground and will be opened (Reverse biased) when a signal is provided to base pin. This is where a PNP transistor differs from a NPN transistor, if you are looking for an equivalent NPN type check out BD135 transistor.

BD136 has a gain value of 40 to 250, this value determines the amplification capacity of the transistor. The maximum amount of current that could flow through the Collector pin is 1.5A, hence we cannot connect loads that consume more than 1.5A using this transistor. To bias a transistor we have to supply current to base pin, this current (IB) should be limited to 5mA and voltage across the base emitter pin should be 5V.

When this transistor is fully biased then it can allow a maximum of 1.5A to flow across the collector and emitter. This stage is called Saturation Region and the typical voltage allowed across the Collector-Emitter (V­CE) or Base-Emitter (VBE) could be 45V and 45V respectively. When base current is removed the transistor becomes fully off, this stage is called as the Cut-off Region and the Base Emitter voltage could be around 500 mV.

The BD136 is a medium power PNP transistor. It can be used to control heavy loads since it has a high collector current value of 1.5A. Another peculiar fact about this transistor is that it comes in plastic package, while most medium power transistor are available only in metal can package. This reduces the cost of the Transistor and also since the package is not conductive it will not be affected by other noise in the circuit. Due to this feature this transistor is widely used in amplifier applications.
So if you are looking for a medium power PNP transistor in Plastic package, then this Transistor might be the right choice for you.

A modern solderless breadboard consists of a perforated block of plastic with numerous tin plated phosphor bronze or nickel silver alloy spring clips under the perforations. The clips are often called tie points or contact points. The number of tie points is often given in the specification of the breadboard.

The spacing between the clips (lead pitch) is typically 0.1" (2.54 mm). Integrated circuits (ICs) in dual in-line packages (DIPs) can be inserted to straddle the centerline of the block. Interconnecting wires and the leads of discrete components (such as capacitors, resistors, and inductors) can be inserted into the remaining free holes to complete the circuit. Where ICs are not used, discrete components and connecting wires may use any of the holes. Typically the spring clips are rated for 1 ampere at 5 volts and 0.333 amperes at 15 volts (5 watts).

blocks.text: General purpose load cell for weight sensing up to 20Kg (Size: 80 x 13 x 13 mm) - to buy additional Weight Scale Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) 24-bit board (HX711)

This straight bar load cell (sometimes called a strain gauge) can translate up to 20kg of pressure (force) into an electrical signal. Each load cell can measure the electrical resistance that changes in response to, and is proportional to, the strain (e.g. pressure or force) applied to the bar. With this gauge, you will be able to tell just how heavy an object is, if an object’s weight changes over time, or if you simply need to sense the presence of an object by measuring strain or load applied to a surface.
Each straight bar load cell is made from an aluminum alloy and is capable of reading a capacity of 20kg. These load cells have four strain gauges that are hooked up in a wheatstone bridge formation.
The load cell acts like a bridge, it has 4 colored wires as follows
Here are some typical technical specifications for a 20kg load cell:
Creep: <0.03% of full scale per minute
How This Load Cell Works: Strain Gauge + Wheatstone Bridge

This straight bar load cell measures weight using four strain gauges bonded to an aluminum alloy bar, wired together in a Wheatstone bridge (the standard configuration for this type of sensor). As weight bends the bar by a tiny, invisible amount, the strain gauges' electrical resistance shifts, and the bridge converts that shift into a small differential voltage signal that changes in proportion to the load. On its own, this signal is too small for a microcontroller to read directly — it needs an ADC amplifier such as the HX711 Weight Scale ADC to boost and digitize it.
Choosing the Right Load Cell Capacity

A load cell 20kg rated like this one is sized for the heaviest object you expect to weigh — going over that rated capacity can damage the strain gauges permanently. If 20kg isn't the right fit for your project, RAM Electronics also stocks:
5kg load cell — for small parcels or kitchen-scale-sized projects.
40kg load cell and 50kg load cell — for mid-range weighing.

As a rule of thumb in load-cell sizing, it's common to choose a rated capacity comfortably above your heaviest expected load rather than right at the limit, to leave headroom and protect the sensor from occasional overloads.
Building a Digital Scale With This Load Cell for Arduino
This load cell for Arduino projects needs just two other parts to become a working digital scale: an HX711 amplifier board and a microcontroller.
Connect the load cell's 4 wires (Signal+, Signal-, VCC, GND, as listed above) to the HX711 board's matching terminals.
Connect the HX711's data and clock lines to two digital pins on an Arduino UNO Rev3 (A65) or Arduino Nano (CH340), plus power and ground.
Load an HX711 library, then calibrate by placing a known weight on the load cell and dividing the reading by that weight to get a calibration factor.
A load cell is a sensor that converts a physical force, like weight, into an electrical signal. This one is a straight-bar type, sometimes also called a strain gauge.
How does a strain gauge load cell work?

Four strain gauges bonded to the bar are wired into a Wheatstone bridge. As the bar flexes slightly under load, the strain gauges' resistance changes, producing a small voltage signal proportional to the applied weight.
What does the wiring color code mean?
On this load cell: VCC is the red wire, GND is the black wire, Signal+ is the green wire, and Signal- is the white wire.
What capacity load cell do I need for my project?
Choose a rated capacity that comfortably covers the heaviest weight you plan to measure — going over the rated capacity can permanently damage the strain gauges.
Does this load cell need an amplifier to work with a microcontroller?
Yes. Its output signal is too small for a microcontroller to read directly, so it needs an ADC amplifier board such as the HX711 to boost and digitize the signal first.
Can this load cell be used with Arduino?
Yes — paired with an HX711 amplifier board, it connects to any Arduino board (or similar microcontroller) over two digital pins.

Building a digital scale for a school STEM project or a workshop tool this term? This load cell 20kg pairs directly with RAM's HX711 amplifier board for a complete weight-sensing setup. Contact RAM Electronics to check availability.

The device is pin-to-pin compatible with common NEC encoder parts, easing redesign or replacement.

The datasheet includes simple application circuits (oscillator/resonator, LED driver resistor and key-matrix wiring) so engineers can move from prototype to production quickly. makers-489143.summary: The IRFP9240 is a -200V P-Channel MOSFET in a TO-247 package with a low 0.34Ω on-resistance. It’s designed for fast switching, is avalanche-rated.

blocks.text: The IRFP9240 is a silicon P-channel enhanced mode power MOSFET, manufactured using advanced MOSFET technology. This technology is focused on optimizing key performance parameters, specifically engineered to significantly reduce conduction losses during operation. The fundamental structure is a vertical DMOS design, which allows it to handle high voltage and current efficiently. As a P-channel device, its voltage polarities and current flow are the inverse of the more common N-channel MOSFETs, making it suitable for specific circuit configurations like high-side switching.

A primary benefit of this transistor’s advanced design is its improved switching performance, making it effective in high-frequency applications. blocks.text: The UNI-T UT516B Insulation Resistance Tester is a handheld instrument engineered to evaluate the integrity of electrical insulation in industrial and commercial environments. Encased in a robust, ergonomically contoured housing, the UT516B integrates a high-contrast backlit LCD display that guides technicians through the insulation test process. At its core, the device seamlessly generates precise DC test voltages, allowing users to monitor the decay of leakage current and assess insulation health. By sequentially delivering controlled voltages and measuring resistance response, the tester computes key diagnostic ratios such as polarization index and dielectric absorption ratio directly on-screen, promoting insightful analysis without external calculation.

Data from each test can be archived in the instrument’s memory bank, enabling longitudinal tracking of insulation degradation over time. The thoughtful arrangement of the rotary dial and function keys ensures quick configuration of test parameters, while built-in alerts notify operators of over-range conditions.

Designed for portability, the tester features durable connectors and a protective rubber boot that resists impacts and environmental wear, making it suitable for field service. With intuitive on-device prompts and the ability to offload stored data via a USB connection, the UT516B fosters efficient workflows, whether verifying new installations or performing routine preventive maintenance, ensuring system reliability.

blocks.text: LM1281N 85MHz RGB Video Amplifier System with On Screen Display (OSD) DIP-28

The LM1281N is a full-feature video amplifier with OSD inputs, all within a 28-pin package. This part is intended for use in monitors with resolutions up to 1024 x 768. The video section of the LM1281 features three matched video amplifiers with blanking. All of the video amplifier Adjustments feature high input impedance 0V to 4V DC controls, providing easy interfacing to bus-controlled alignment systems. The OSD section features three TTL inputs and a DC contrast control. The switching between the OSD and video section is controlled by a single TTL input. Although the OSD signals are TTL inputs, these signals are internally processed to match the OSD logic low level to the video black level. When adjusting the drive controls for color balance of the video signal, the color balance of the OSD display will track these color adjustments. The LM1281N also features an internal spot-killer circuit to protect the CRT when the monitor is turned off.

blocks.text: Note:?Complete Technical Details can be found in the datasheet present at the end of this page.
The BT136 is TRIAC with 4A maximum terminal current. The gate threshold voltage of the BT136 is also very less so can be driven by digital circuits.

Since TRIACs are bi-directional switching devices they are commonly used for switching AC applications. So if you looking to switch of control (dim, speed control) an AC load which consumes less than 6A with a digital device like microcontroller or microprocessor then BT136 might be the right for you.

There are many different ways to use a TRIAC, since the device is bi-directional the TRIAC gate can be trigger with either positive voltage or negative voltage. So this allows the TIRAC to be operated in four different modes. You can read this?article?if you want to know more about the switching modes. A simple TRIAC switching circuit is shown below.

In this circuit the TRIAC can be turned using the switch, when the switch is pressed the TRIAC closes the connection for the AC bulb though the AC mains. For this to happen, the gate pin of the TRIAC should receive a voltage greater than the threshold gate voltage and should also get a current that is greater than gate trigger current. This will make the TRIAC turn on.

Since the TRIAC and SCR share most of the same characteristics, just like SCR the TRIAC will also not turn off when the gate voltage is removed. We need special type of circuit called commutation circuit to turn of the SCR again. This commutation is normally done by reducing the load current (forced commutation) less than the holding current. To put it simple the TRIAC will remain turned on only till the load current is greater than the holding current of the TRIAC.
Note:?Commutation is not required in AC switching circuits because the TRIAC will not latch in on state since the AC voltage reaches zero for every half cycle.

Other than controlling through switch the BT136 can also be controlled through a microcontroller or a microprocessor. To do this we need an Opto-isolator like?MOC3021?to isolate the AC circuit form Digital electronics. This way the Load can not only be switched but also the output coltage can be controlled by using PWM signals for fast switching.
Since TRIACS deal with AC voltages, the circuit involving them has to be designed properly to aboid problem some tips are shared below

All TRIAC circuits suffer from an effect called Rate Effect. This occurs when the TRIAC is switching frequently and a sudden high voltage occurs at either main terminal of the TRIAC and damages the TRIAC itself. It can be avoided by using a snubber circuit.

Similarly there is another effect called backlash effect. This occurs due to the capacitance that gets accumulated between the two terminals of the MT1 and MT2 of the TRIAC. Due to this the TRIAC will not turn on even if the gate voltage is applied. This problem can be solved by providing a resistance in series for the capacitance to discharge.
When controlling the output AC voltage for dimmer or speed control applications a Zero crossing method is always recommended to be used.
In switching circuits the TRIAC is easily subjected to harmonics and EMI interference hence should be isolated from other digital electronics.
There is chance of backward current when the TRIAC is switching inductive loads, so an alternate discharge path has to be provided for the load to drain the inrush current.

More technical details and LM386 specifications can be found in the LM386 datasheet attached at the bottom of the article.
Where to use the LM386 Audio Amplifier

The LM386 is a low power audio frequency amplifier which is very commonly used in small audio amplifiers. The IC consumes very less power and hence can be operated using a 9V battery easily. It can easily drive an 8-ohm speaker with a variable gain of 20 to200. Volume control and gain control is also possible in this. The IC comes in a 8-pin PDIP package and requires very less components to function hence it is highly easy to use.

So, if you are looking for an audio amplifier IC which can be powered using a battery for a portable application to drive an 8-ohm speaker then this IC might be the right choice for you. For driving heavy speakers you have to use the power amplifier ICs.
The LM386 only requires a couple of capacitors and resistors to start working. A very basic commonly used LM386 circuit is shown below.

The IC is powered using the pin 6 (typically 5 or 9V) and the ground pin 4 is connected to the ground. The inverting pin (pin 2) is normally grounded and the Non-inverting pin (pin 3) is provided with the Audio signal. This audio signal can be from a microphone or even from a 3.5mm jack. The 10k resistor is added in series with the audio signal to act as a volume control. You can ignore this potentiometer if you want to operate in full volume.

The pin 1 and pin 8 are used to set the gain of the Amplifier. If there is nothing connected between these pins then the default gain will be 26 dB, but we can connect a 10 µF capacitor across it to get the maximum in of the IC which is 46dB. The pin 7 is used to connect a filtering capacitor (0.1uf) for our amplifier IC to avoid unnecessary oscillations. The amplified audio signal can be obtained from the pin 5 which is connected to a 8-ohm speaker through a filtering capacitor. The RC network with 0.05uF and 10k resistor is optional.

blocks.text: Note: Complete Technical Details can be found at the MPSA42 datasheet given at the end of this page.

MPSA42 is a NPN transistor hence the collector and emitter will be left open (Reverse biased) when the base pin is held at ground and will be closed (Forward biased) when a signal is provided to base pin. It has a gain value of 30; this value determines the amplification capacity of the transistor, normally MPSA42 will not be used for amplification due to its low gain value. The maximum amount of current that could flow through the Collector pin is 500mA, hence we cannot drive loads that consume more than 500mA using this transistor. To bias a transistor, we have to supply current to base pin, this current (IB) should be limited to 5mA.

When this transistor is fully biased, then it can allow a maximum of 500mA to flow across the collector and emitter. This stage is called Saturation Region and the typical voltage allowed across the Collector-Emitter (V­CE) or Collector-Base (VCB) could be 300V and 300V respectively. When base current is removed the transistor becomes fully off, this stage is called as the Cut-off Region.

The MPSA42 is a high voltage NPN transistor. A transistor can normally be used as a switch or amplifier, but this transistor is commonly used only for switching purpose since it has a low gain value of 30. The MPSA42 can turn on or turn off high voltage loads (upto 300V) hence they are commonly used for heavy loads or loads that have high peak voltage. Also note that the collector current of the IC is 500mA (0.5A) hence you cannot drive loads which might consume high current. It has a Base-Emitter voltage of 6V hence it can be controlled easily using microcontrollers or other digital electronics.
So if you are looking for an NPN transistor that could switch high voltages with a decent current flow, then the MPSA42 transistor might be the right choice.

MPSA42 transistor is normally used to switch high voltage loads or loads that have high peak voltages. When a transistor is used as a switch it is operated in the Saturation and Cut-Off Region as explained above. As discussed a transistor will act as an Open switch during Forward Bias and as a closed switch during Reverse Bias, this biasing can be achieved by supplying the required amount of current to the base pin. As mentioned the biasing current should maximum of 5mA. Anything more than 5mA will kill the Transistor; hence a resistor is always added in series with base pin. The value of this resistor (RB) can be calculated using below formulae.

In the below circuit we have used the MPSA42 transistor to control a high voltage (48V) motor. The resistance (RB) can be calculated using the above formulae as we know the VBE is 5V in this circuit and IB is 5mA. So RB is (5/0.005) 1000ohms (1K)

When +5V is supplied, the base current flows through the current limiting 1K resistor to the base pin, the transistor is forward biased and thus the motor is connected to ground. If 0V is supplied to base pin, no current flows to base and thus the transistor is reversed biased making the motor to stop. Also note that the operating current of the motor is just 0.4A which is less than the collector continuous current (0.5A) of the transistor.

📏 Mixer-style form factor: 88 mm body length with 15 mm width and 8 mm thickness gives a slim profile for tight channel strips.

⚙️ Divider wiring: Connect outer pins (A and B) to your reference rails; take the wiper (W) as the control voltage.

🛠️ Mechanical lugs: Solder the 2 mounting lugs to their plated holes to lock the fader to the PCB; they are not part of the resistor network.
🧲 Panel slot & travel: Size the panel slot to cover full travel; keep the carriage parallel to prevent rail rub.

What do the extra 2 pins do? They’re mechanical lugs for fixing the fader to the PCB; they have no electrical function.
What does B10K mean? Linear taper (B) with 10 kΩ total resistance.
Is “103” the same value? Yes — 103 is the standard code for 10 kΩ.
Can I read it with a microcontroller? Yes — wire as a voltage divider and read the wiper with an ADC.

blocks.text: WAGO NC-221 Wire Connector 1 In 1 Out – Compact Spring Lever Cable Connector
WAGO NC-221 Wire Connector 1 In 1 Out

The WAGO NC-221 Wire Connector is a compact and practical wiring solution designed for users who need a quick, secure, and organized method for connecting wires in low-voltage electrical systems. With its 1 input and 1 output configuration, this connector is ideal for direct inline wire connection where reliable contact, easy handling, and compact size are important.

This WAGO wire connector uses a spring lever clamping mechanism, allowing wires to be inserted and secured quickly without twisting, soldering, or using traditional screw terminals. This helps reduce installation time, simplifies maintenance work, and makes rewiring much easier whenever modifications are needed. The lever design also provides strong and stable pressure on the conductor for dependable long-term performance.

One of the key advantages of the WAGO NC-221 is its modular snap-together design. Multiple identical connectors can be connected side by side, giving the user a flexible way to expand the wiring arrangement as needed. This makes it especially practical in projects where scalable wiring layouts or grouped parallel connections are required.

Its compact free-hanging design makes it suitable for use in lighting connections, electrical distribution boxes, control panels, switchboards, HVAC wiring, home automation systems, and testing setups. The transparent-style housing helps users inspect wire insertion visually, while the flame-retardant construction improves safety and durability during use.

Because it combines fast lever operation, reusable connection, compact size, and scalable installation, the WAGO NC-221 is an excellent choice for electricians, technicians, installers, maintenance users, and DIY projects that need neat and dependable wire connection.

ومن المميزات المهمة في WAGO NC-221 أنه يمكن تجميع أكثر من قطعة بجانب بعضها عن طريق تثبيت الوحدات المتشابهة معًا، مما يتيح للمستخدم تكوين ترتيب توصيل مرن وقابل للتوسعة حسب الحاجة. وهذه الميزة تجعل المنتج مناسبًا للتطبيقات التي تحتاج إلى تنظيم أكثر من خط داخل مساحة عملية صغيرة.

التصميم المدمج لهذا الموصل يجعله مناسبًا للاستخدام في أنظمة الإضاءة، وصناديق التوصيل، ولوحات التحكم، ولوحات التوزيع، وأنظمة التكييف، والمشاريع المنزلية، وتجارب الاختبار والتوصيل السريع. كما أن جسم الموصل مصنوع من مادة مقاومة للاشتعال، مما يساعد على رفع مستوى الأمان أثناء الاستخدام، بينما تساهم خامة نقاط التلامس الداخلية في توفير توصيل كهربائي جيد وثابت.

إذا كنت تحتاج إلى موصل أسلاك WAGO صغير وسريع وآمن لتوصيل خط واحد بشكل مباشر، فإن WAGO NC-221 يقدم حلًا عمليًا يجمع بين سهولة الاستخدام، وثبات التوصيل، وإمكانية إعادة الاستخدام، وإمكانية التوسعة بإضافة وحدات مماثلة.

12.6V 35Ah High Drain Rechargeable Lithium-ion Battery Pack

The 12.6V 35Ah High Drain Rechargeable Battery Pack is built for users who need a powerful and dependable energy source for demanding 12V applications. With a large 35Ah capacity and a strong 40A maximum discharge current, this battery pack is ideal for systems that require both long runtime and stable high-current output.

Designed in a 3S12P lithium-ion configuration, this battery uses a robust multi-cell structure that helps distribute current more effectively across the pack. This improves stability during operation, supports better thermal behavior, and helps the battery maintain consistent performance under demanding loads. It is especially suitable for applications where ordinary battery packs may not provide enough endurance or output capability.

Its high-capacity design makes it an excellent choice for portable fridges, field lighting systems, motor-driven projects, backup power units, communication equipment, and other portable or fixed 12V systems. Whether used in outdoor setups, engineering projects, workshop applications, or emergency backup solutions, this battery pack provides a practical combination of high energy storage, strong output, and rechargeable convenience.

The integrated protection system adds another important advantage by helping protect the battery and connected devices from overcharge, over-discharge, short circuit, and excessive current conditions. This improves operational safety and helps extend the practical service life of the battery.

For users who need a rechargeable 12.6V high drain battery with larger capacity and dependable 40A performance, this battery pack offers a balanced solution for both professional and advanced DIY use.

بطارية ليثيوم أيون قابلة لإعادة الشحن 12.6 فولت 35 أمبير

تم تصميم بطارية 12.6 فولت 35 أمبير تفريغ عالي لتلبية احتياجات المستخدمين الذين يبحثون عن مصدر طاقة قوي وموثوق للتطبيقات التي تتطلب سعة كبيرة مع قدرة ممتازة على توفير التيار. بفضل السعة الكبيرة 35 أمبير وأقصى تيار تفريغ يصل إلى 40 أمبير، تعد هذه البطارية خيارًا مناسبًا للأنظمة التي تحتاج إلى تشغيل لفترات أطول مع الحفاظ على خرج ثابت تحت الأحمال المرتفعة.

تعتمد البطارية على تكوين 3S12P، وهو تصميم قوي يساعد على توزيع الحمل الكهربائي بشكل أفضل بين الخلايا، مما يدعم استقرار الأداء أثناء التشغيل ويُحسّن من التعامل مع التطبيقات التي تحتاج إلى تيار مرتفع بشكل مستمر. كما يساهم هذا التكوين في تحسين التوازن الحراري ودعم الاعتمادية العملية عند استخدام البطارية في المشاريع أو الأنظمة التي تعمل تحت حمل فعلي.

تُعد هذه البطارية مناسبة لتطبيقات كثيرة مثل الثلاجات المحمولة، وأنظمة الإضاءة عالية القدرة، ومشاريع الروبوتات، وبعض التطبيقات المعتمدة على المحركات، وأجهزة الاتصال، وأنظمة الطاقة الاحتياطية. كما أنها مناسبة للمستخدمين الذين يحتاجون إلى بطارية قابلة لإعادة الشحن بجهد 12.6 فولت تجمع بين السعة العالية، وثبات الأداء، وسهولة الدمج في المشاريع المختلفة.

وتحتوي البطارية على نظام حماية داخلي يساعد في حماية البطارية والأجهزة المتصلة بها من الشحن الزائد، والتفريغ الزائد، وزيادة التيار، والقصر الكهربائي، مما يدعم مستوى الأمان أثناء الاستخدام ويحسن من موثوقية التشغيل على المدى العملي.
إذا كنت تحتاج إلى بطارية قوية قابلة لإعادة الشحن لتطبيقات 12 فولت التي تتطلب قدرة عالية وسعة كبيرة وأداء ثابت، فإن هذه البطارية تمثل اختيارًا عمليًا واحترافيًا للعديد من الاستخدامات.

blocks.text: MAX7219 LED Dot Matrix 4 In 1 Display with 5P Line Module Red
This is Dot Led Matrix Module incorporating MAX7219 Driver chip. By using this dot LED module in your upcoming project, you will be able to add some great cool animation.

The individual module features 8×8 LED’s, each controlled very precisely by the MAX7219 driver to generate the colour pattern you wish. The great advantage of using this is users will have control over all of the 64 LED by just connecting 3 output communication wires to microcontrollers like Arduino etc.
This product has 4 Dot Matrix LED’s cascaded to form a single LED Display to allot more area to the user on the display.

The MAX7219 Dot Led Matrix Module is a serial input common-cathode driver that interfaces micro-controllers to LED matrices. All common micro-controllers can be connected to this module by using a 4-wire serial interface. Each output can be addressed without refreshing the entire display. This module requires only 3 I/O lines for driving the display, making it ideal for your microcontroller projects. Only one external register is used to set the segment current of each LED.

Streamline IC rework with this 4-piece Debonding Brush Heads Set engineered for motherboard chip glue/underfill removal. 2N3819 is a general-purpose N-channel Junction Field Effect Transistor. It operates in depletion-mode and requires reverse biasing to turn off. It is designed for medium to high range frequencies. Furthermore, it has a high gain for wideband frequencies and has an importance in VHF/UHF based systems. It is a small-signal device capable of fast switching, signal amplification, and mixing in low noise applications.
This tutorial will discuss its pinout, configuration, features, specifications, example circuits, 2D model, and its applications.
Following is the pinout of the 2N3819 N-Channel JFET:
This epitaxial silicon transistor has three pins. The leftmost pin is the source, and the rightmost numbered as 3, is the drain pin. The middle pin serves as the gate of the JFET.
The pin configuration detail in tabular is mentioned below:
Gate-Source Cut off voltage (Vds=15 Volts,Ig=10 nA) : -8.0Volts
Gate-Source Breakdown voltage (Vds=0 Volts,Ig=1.0 uA) : 25 Volts
Zero Gate Voltage Drain Current (15Volts,Vgs=0Volts) : 2.0 – 20 mA
The most important point to note here is that it can provide only 100mA drain current. Therefore, you should it as a switch only when required drain current is less than 100mA.
For more information about the technical details and small-signal characteristics, check the 2N3819 datasheet. The link to the datasheet is provided at the bottom of the article.

This N-channel JFET can be used for low side switching only. Because N-channel FETs are used to drive low-side power paths only. But if you want to drive a high-side load, you can use any other P-channel JFET. Another important point here to note here is that the drain current of 2N3819 JFET is 100mA. Hence, it will be used for an application that only requires less than 100mA Drain current.
In this section, circuits based on 2N3819 N-Channel JFET will be discussed.
The following circuit shows the example of 2N3819 JFET as a switch. A DC voltmeter is connected between Drain and sourcr terminal to measure voltage across Drain terminal.

When zero voltage is applied to the Gate terminal of N-channel JFET, FET operates in saturation mode and It acts like a closed circuit and almost zero voltage appears across the Drain terminal as you can see on the DC voltmeter.

Similarly, when enough negative voltage is applied to Gate terminal of N-channel JFET, FET operates in the cut-off region and It acts as an open circuit and input voltage source (+25V) appears across Drain terminal as you can see on the DC voltmeter.
The circuitry for an AC field detector is shown above:

It will explain the working of 2N3819 N-Channel JFET as a field detector. The transistor source terminal is connected with 6-12 Volts of power source to supply voltage to 555 Timer IC. The IC is further connected with an LED, which brightens when the timer turns on, and a buzzer that produces sound whenever a signal is detected. An antenna is connected to the gate of 2N3819 to detect the AC field. Whenever the antenna senses a charge or a wave, it will induce a voltage and pass it to the gate terminal. The change in the gate voltage alters ID and activates the Timer IC. As a result, the led starts to blink, showing the activation of the IC, and the buzzer produces the sound to indicate that a charge is detected by the antenna.
An audio mixer is a device used to amplify and mix audio signals to produce different sounds and enhance audio quality. The schematic of an audio mixer is as shown :

The transistor gate is linked with two audio input channels, followed by coupling capacitors and variable resistors. N-Channel JFETs have high gain. The working of a mixer is similar to that of an amplifier except for the variable resistors’ part. When input signals are applied, gate voltage changes, the drain current changes, which in return varies the voltage drop across the load resistor, performing amplification of the audio signal.

The variable resistors play their role in the mixing of audios. By varying the resistances, we can control the contribution of each input channel in the output mixed and amplified signal. This results in various levels of sounds. The output is coupled with a capacitor so that the resultant signal is a fine quality signal.

ekostra-14242.summary: Single-layer copper-clad board for custom PCB etching FR2 (phenolic paper) base material, easy to cut and drill Standard 100×100mm (10×10 cm²) prototyping size Easy to cut, drill, and etch for DIY circuit designs Bare copper finish for full customization Great for prototyping, educational use, and soldering practice

blocks.text: This 10 x 10 cm single-sided copper clad board is a blank FR2 (phenolic paper) PCB laminate for making your own printed circuit boards. One side is covered with bare copper, ready for toner transfer and etching, photo-resist or CNC milling, so you can turn a circuit design into a real, neat board at home, in the lab or at school.
Layers: single-sided (copper on one side only)
Clean the copper with fine sandpaper or steel wool, then wipe it with alcohol until it is bright.
Print the mirrored layout on glossy paper with a laser printer and iron it onto the copper.
Soak the board in water, peel the paper off and touch up any missing tracks with a permanent marker.
Etch in ferric chloride until the uncovered copper is gone, then rinse with water.
Remove the toner with acetone, drill the holes (0.8 to 1mm suits most components) and solder.
Ferric chloride is corrosive and stains: wear gloves and eye protection, work in a ventilated place and do not pour used etchant down the drain.
Wear a mask when cutting, sanding or drilling the board, as the dust irritates the lungs and skin.
Cut the board with a hacksaw, or score both sides deeply along a ruler and snap it.

ekostra-13593.summary: 🔌 CH340/CH340T USB-to-Serial adapter for Arduino & modules 📡 Includes NRF24L01 2.4GHz wireless transceiver module ⚡ Easy serial communication for programming and debugging 🛰️ NRF24L01 supports low-power wireless data links 🧩 Ideal for wireless sensor networks and remote control projects 🚌 Works great with Arduino, ESP32, STM32 (with proper wiring) 🛠️ Plug-and-play USB serial interface (driver may be needed) ✅ Great bundle for quick RF experiments and prototyping

blocks.text: This bundle combines a CH340/CH340T USB-to-serial adapter with an NRF24L01 2.4GHz wireless transceiver module. Plugged into a computer, the CH340 appears as a virtual COM port, so a PC program or serial terminal can exchange data with Arduino projects and wireless sensor nodes over a low-power 2.4GHz radio link. It is a convenient set for RF experiments, remote data logging and wireless control from a PC.
USB chip: CH340 / CH340T, USB 2.0 to TTL serial (virtual COM port)
RF data rate: 250 kbps, 1 Mbps or 2 Mbps (NRF24L01)
Install the CH340 driver if your computer does not show a new COM port after plugging in.
Find the COM port number (Device Manager on Windows).
Open a serial terminal, such as the Arduino Serial Monitor, at the adapter’s baud rate.
On the other side, the second NRF24L01 (for example on an Arduino) must use the same channel, address and data rate as the adapter.
Wireless serial link between a PC and an Arduino project
Collecting data from wireless sensor nodes on a PC
Remote control of robots and devices from a computer
When you connect an NRF24L01 to an Arduino, power it from 3.3V, never 5V (its supply range is 1.9V to 3.6V). Its signal pins accept 5V logic.
A 10µF capacitor across the NRF24L01 VCC and GND pins makes the link much more stable.
Range depends on the antenna, walls and nearby Wi-Fi traffic; test at short distance first.
1 x CH340/CH340T USB to serial adapter with NRF24L01 2.4GHz module
